spatial.description: These questions are about spatial relationships, such as nearby objects or objects in particular directions.
examples: What is the bottle near to the table?
Which box is closest to the window?
What is to the left of the toilet?
Which bucket is to the right of the bin?
What is the bottle close to the shower?
What is in front of the bin?
What is behind the stool?
What is between the toilet and the sink?
What is inside the cupboard?
What is to the right of the chair and behind the air conditioner?

support.description: These questions are about support relationships, such as which objects support each other and how they do so.
examples: Which bottle is on the table?
What does the shower curtain hang from?
Which clothes hanger is on the radiator?
What supports the clothes hanger?
What is attached to the wall?
What is hanging on the door?
What supports the bottle?
Which jumper is lying on the bed?

semantic.description: These questions are about properties of the objects, such as their size, shape, color, and texture.
examples: Where is the largest bottle in the room?
What is the most red object?
What is the smallest bucket in the room?
Which pillow is heart shaped?
Which door is half open?
What wall has been written on?
Which table is circuler?
Which computer is new?
What is the most comfortable chair in the room?
Which table is the cleanest?
Which sofa is white?
Which sofa has the same texture as the chair?
What is the most comfortable chair to sit in?
Which object on the table can be read?
Which washing machine is on?
